title: commit-sync scans only commit subjects, so body-referenced stories are never linked or transitioned

description:
## What

`story commit-sync` scans commits with `git log --format='%H %s'` — subject
lines only. A story referenced anywhere in a commit **body** is invisible to
it, so it gets no `[git]` comment and never auto-transitions from the default
open state to the `active` one.

This is the same defect class as SH-56, in a different code path. SH-56 covers
`POST_MERGE_HOOK` (auto-close) in `src/hooks.rs`; this is `commit-sync` itself
(comment linking + auto-transition) in `src/app.rs`. Fixing one does not fix
the other.

## Where

`src/app.rs`, `Invocation::CommitSync`:

    let output = std::process::Command::new("git")
        .args(["log", "--format=%H %s", &format!("--since={since_date}")])

`%s` is the subject alone. Everything downstream — `extract_story_ids`, the
`[git] <hash>: <subject>` comment, and the `todo -> in-progress` transition —
only ever sees that one line.

## Why it breaks

CLAUDE.md mandates Conventional Commits for this repo, whose subject line is
reserved for a concise summary under 72 characters. Story references
consequently land in the body. So, as with SH-56, following the project's own
commit style guarantees the feature does nothing.

The blast radius is wider than SH-56's, because `commit-sync` runs from the
managed `post-commit` hook on **every commit**, not just on merges.

## Extent / repro

In a scratch repo (`story init --prefix CS`, two stories, hooks not required):

    git commit -m "feat: something for CS-1"                    # subject reference
    git commit -m "feat: something else" -m "Closes CS-2"       # body trailer

    $ story commit-sync --since 1h
    scanned 3 commits, added 1 comments to 1 stories
    CS-1: todo -> in-progress (referenced in 84fae18)

CS-1 got its comment and its transition. CS-2 got neither, and stayed `todo`.

Reproduced against v0.17.0 (2026-07-26).

## Last known good

None. `--format=%H %s` is present in the original implementation, so body
references have plausibly never been linked.

## Fix

Not a one-token swap — this is where it differs from SH-56. `%B` emits
multi-line records, and the parser is line-oriented:

    for line in log_output.lines() {
        let (hash, message) = match line.split_once(' ') { ... };

With `%B`, a body line like `Closes CS-2` parses as hash=`Closes`,
message=`CS-2`, producing a `[git] Closes: CS-2` comment. That is worse than
the current miss: the short hash is the idempotency key
(`comment_prefix = format!("[git] {short_hash}:")`), so a garbage hash also
breaks the "safe to run repeatedly" guarantee.

Use a record-separated format and parse per commit rather than per line, e.g.

    --format=%H%x1f%B%x1e

splitting on `\x1e` for commits and `\x1f` for hash/message. Keep the comment
text as the subject alone (the first line of `%B`) — a comment carrying an
entire multi-paragraph body would be unreadable in `story show`.

Verify: a body reference is linked; a commit referencing two stories links
both; the same commit scanned twice still adds one comment.

## Preventative action

`commit-sync` has no test that exercises real `git log` output against a real
repo. `tests/story_sync_git.rs` exists — extend it with a case whose reference
is in the body, which pins both this bug and the parsing trap above.

## Related, but separate

`story help commit-sync` claims it "auto-transitions stories based on commit
patterns (e.g., 'closes SH-1')". There is no close-pattern handling in
`Invocation::CommitSync` at all — the only transition is
default-open -> `role = "active"`, triggered by any reference regardless of
wording. Either the docs overstate the feature or the feature is missing; worth
deciding, but it is a distinct defect from this one and is not filed here.
